name: Justin Sun

summary.text: Justin Sun is the founder of the Tron blockchain and the owner of Rainberry Inc. (formerly BitTorrent). In March 2023 the SEC sued him and three of his companies in the Southern District of New York for unregistered offers and sales of the TRX and BTT tokens and for alleged manipulative wash trading and undisclosed celebrity touting. In February 2025 the SEC and Sun jointly asked the court to stay the case; in March 2026 a final judgment imposed a $10 million civil penalty on Rainberry and dismissed the claims against Sun, the Tron Foundation and the BitTorrent Foundation. Sun bought about $75 million of World Liberty Financial's WLFI token in 2024-25 and was named an adviser; he said in May 2025 that he was the largest holder of the $TRUMP memecoin and attended the May 22, 2025 dinner for its top holders at Trump National Golf Club. In 2026 he and World Liberty Financial sued each other after the company froze his wallet.

facts.claim: On March 22, 2023 the SEC filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (No. 23-cv-2433) against Justin Sun, Tron Foundation Limited, BitTorrent Foundation Ltd. and Rainberry Inc., alleging unregistered offers and sales of the TRX and BTT tokens through bounty programs and airdrops in violation of Section 5 of the Securities Act, and alleging that Sun orchestrated wash trading to inflate TRX's apparent trading volume and paid celebrities to promote the tokens without disclosure. The complaint alleged violations of Sections 17(a)(1) and (3) of the Securities Act and Sections 9(a)(1), 9(a)(2) and 10(b) of the Exchange Act.
facts.quote: The SEC's complaint, filed March 22, 2023 in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleged that crypto entrepreneur Justin Sun and three of his wholly-owned companies engaged in unregistered offers and sales of TRX and BTT.

sources.title: Justin Sun et al. - Litigation Release No. 25676
SEC Charges Crypto Entrepreneur Justin Sun and His Companies for Fraud and Other Securities Law Violations
Complaint, SEC v. Sun et al.

facts.claim: On February 26, 2025 the SEC, Sun, the Tron Foundation and the related defendants filed a joint motion asking the court to stay the case while they explored a potential resolution, proposing to file a joint status report within 60 days if the stay was granted. The motion said a resolution would avoid the need for the court to rule on the defendants' pending motion to dismiss.
facts.quote: The motion argued that a resolution would conserve judicial resources by obviating the need for the Court to resolve the Defendants' pending motion to dismiss the complaint.

sources.title: SEC, Justin Sun, Tron Ask Court to Pause Fraud Case Over 'Potential Resolution'

Securities and Exchange Commission v. Sun, 1:23-cv-02433

facts.claim: In March 2026 the case was resolved by a final judgment under which Rainberry Inc. agreed, without admitting or denying the allegations, to pay a $10 million civil penalty and to a permanent injunction, and the SEC dismissed with prejudice its claims against Justin Sun, the Tron Foundation and the BitTorrent Foundation. The court docket lists the case as terminated on March 9, 2026, and an SEC whistleblower notice lists a qualifying judgment or order dated March 9, 2026.
facts.quote: Rainberry shall make this payment within 30 days after entry of this Final Judgment.

facts.claim: Sun bought $30 million of World Liberty Financial's WLFI tokens in November 2024 and was named an adviser to the project the next day; in January 2025 he announced a further $45 million purchase, bringing his total to about $75 million and making him the project's largest investor at the time.
facts.quote: He announced the additional $45 million on January 19, and the new funds brought his total investment in the platform to $75 million, making him its largest investor.

sources.title: Justin Sun Raises Stake in World Liberty Financial to $75M

facts.claim: On May 20, 2025 Sun said publicly that he was the largest holder of the $TRUMP memecoin and would attend the May 22 dinner at Trump National Golf Club outside Washington for the token's top 220 holders. CNBC put his $TRUMP holdings at about $18.6 million, on top of his $75 million in World Liberty Financial. The dinner had been announced on gettrumpmemes.com on April 23, 2025, with rankings based on time-weighted holdings between April 23 and May 12 and a separate reception for the top 25 holders.
facts.quote: Sun announced he will attend Thursday evening's dinner at Mr. Trump's D.C.-area golf club, which is open to the 220 largest holders of the $TRUMP meme coin.

facts.claim: At the White House briefing on May 22, 2025, press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president was attending the memecoin dinner in his 'personal time' and that it was not a White House dinner and was not taking place at the White House; asked whether the attendee list would be published, she said she would raise the question. NPR reported the dinner was held that evening at Trump National Golf Club in Potomac Falls, Virginia.
facts.quote: She responded that the president is attending in his personal time, and it is not a White House dinner, nor taking place at the White House

sources.title: Karoline Leavitt Says You'll Never Know Who's at Trump's Crypto Dinner
Raising ethics questions, top Trump meme coin investors to dine with president tonight

facts.claim: A Bloomberg analysis of the $TRUMP leaderboard as of early May 2025 found that most of the top 25 wallets, with six exceptions, had used offshore exchanges that exclude U.S. customers, and that at least 56 percent of the top 220 wallets had done so, suggesting that most of the top buyers competing for dinner seats were likely outside the United States. Bloomberg noted that some U.S. holders could have used VPNs and that attendees were identified only by self-chosen usernames.

facts.claim: After the dinner Sun said he had received a Trump-branded watch, which he valued at $100,000, as the top holder, and he posted a video of himself entering the Eisenhower Executive Office Building; the White House did not respond to a question about whom he met there. On May 23, 2025 Sun defended the token, saying critics who called it bribery were misguided.

facts.claim: In September 2025 World Liberty Financial used a blacklist function in its smart contract to freeze Sun's wallet. Sun sued the company on April 21, 2026 in the Northern District of California alleging fraud and breach of contract; in May 2026 World Liberty Financial sued Sun for defamation, alleging short selling and straw purchases, which Sun denied. Neither suit had been decided per these sources.

openQuestions: The order granting the February 2025 stay was not itself opened; one secondary report says Judge Edgardo Ramos granted it the next day, and the docket shows a joint status letter to Judge Ramos dated June 26, 2025. The owner should confirm the stay order on the SDNY docket (1:23-cv-02433).

Reports differ on whether the March 2026 final judgment was entered by the court or was still a proposed judgment at the time of writing; the docket's March 9, 2026 termination date and the SEC's whistleblower notice support entry, but the signed order was not opened.
Sun's $100,000 valuation of the watch and the Eisenhower Executive Office Building visit rest on his own posts as relayed by secondary outlets; no White House account of the visit was found.

The Bloomberg leaderboard analysis is an inference from wallet activity, not confirmed nationalities; the 76 percent-of-value figure cited by some secondary outlets was not confirmed against the Bloomberg piece itself.
